[Ubisoft] Ubisoft Entertainment SA (; French: [ybisɔft]; formerly Ubi Soft Entertainment SA) is a French video game publisher headquartered in Saint-Mandé with development studios across the world. Its video game franchises include Anno, Assassin's Creed, Driver, Far Cry, Just Dance, Prince of Persia, Rabbids, Rayman, Tom Clancy's, and Watch Dogs. The company was initially founded in 1984 by Yves Guillemot, who continues to serve as its chairman and CEO, and his four brothers to provide computing software for the French agricultural sector, but moved into the more lucrative sector of video games by 1987. Its first achieved commercial and critical success was the 1995 platform game Rayman, allowing the company to expand worldwide, particularly in Shanghai, Canada, and other European countries. In the early 2000s, Ubisoft acquired the Tom Clancy's and Prince of Persia series, the later which ultimately led to creation of the Assassin's Creed series and other open world game series like Far Cry. The company successfully fended off a hostile takeover by French media conglomerate Vivendi by 2018, part of which came from Chinese media company Tencent acquiring a portion of company shares. Tencent continued to invest in Ubisoft through the 2020s, and further increased their investment to give the Guillimots and Tencent majority control of the company as to prevent a shareholder takeover. With the larger investment from Tencent, Ubisoft underwent a major reorganisation in January 2026, dividing the company amount five creative houses, including Vantage Studios and Massive Entertainment, each overseeing specific series and organised to act self-sufficiently from the larger company.

[Gameloft] Gameloft SE is a French video game company based in Paris, founded in December 1999 by Ubisoft co-founder Michel Guillemot. The company operates 10 development studios worldwide, and publishes games for mobile devices, video game consoles, and PC. The group is known for numerous successful video games and franchises on mobile and, in recent years, on PC and consoles, from Asphalt to Disney Dreamlight Valley. Formerly a public company traded at the Paris Bourse, Gameloft was acquired by French investment company Vivendi in 2016. The group successfully diversified into PC and console games in addition to the mobile market starting in 2022.
